input: Control Device Fabrication: By refining specific fabrication parameters, a perovskite solar cell was assembled, culminating in performance metrics including a PCE of 23.2049%, FF of 76.0187%, Voc of 1.15442 V, and Jsc of 26.4422 mA/cm². The 1.65 mol/L perovskite solution (Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87I3) was prepared, shaken overnight to fully dissolve, and then used to prepare perovskite films. SAM material 4,4,4-NA (0.5 mg/mL) was added to influence crystal growth at the interface and optimize surface passivation. The addition of MACl (15.0 mg/mL) and p-F-PEACl (2.0 mg/mL) as additives were carefully prepared. The perovskite precursor solution was then spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s followed by an additional spin at 5500 rpm for 30 s. At the 15 s of the second step, 150 µL antisolvent was slowly dripped onto the center of the film at 15 s before the end of the spinning program. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 15 min for perovskite crystal formation. A passivation layer, PDADI (0.5 mg/mL) and PiPI (0.15 mg/mL), was incorporated into the system. The passivation solution was spin-coated at 5000 rpm for 30 s on top of the perovskite film to form a passivation layer. At 6 s, a drop of 70 µL passivator was introduced during spin-coating. Thermal treatment involved annealing at 100 °C for 5 min to facilitate crystallization. In details, SAM solution was spin-coated on the substrate at 3000 rpm for 30 s, and annealed at 100 °C for 10 min..
